name: cp
plain: `cp` makes a copy of a file or folder. The original stays; you get a second one with the new name or in a new place.
To copy a folder you must say -r (recursive), or it refuses. To keep timestamps, permissions and ownership, use -a (archive).
when: Back up a file before editing it.
Copy a file into another directory.
Preserve metadata when copying evidence or system files.

examples.title: Copy a folder
examples.explain: -r copies the folder and everything inside it.

examples.title: Archive copy that keeps everything
examples.explain: -a = -r plus preserving permissions, owners, timestamps and symlinks. The safe choice for backups.

examples.title: Ask before overwriting
examples.explain: -i asks y/n if the target exists. -n never overwrites, -u only copies if the source is newer.

examples.title: Make a backup of the target
examples.explain: If dir/file.txt exists it is renamed to file.txt.~1~ before the new copy is placed.

examples.title: Copy and keep timestamps
examples.explain: -p keeps mode, owner and timestamps, but not folder structure.
